I should start by apologizing and acknowledging the issue. Next, I need to explain that our Service Level Agreement (SLA) is calculated monthly, and to receive credits, a formal claim is necessary. rounds.response: I’m really sorry for the interruption and understand why you’re frustrated — we take Enterprise Plus reliability seriously. Three hours of impact would exceed the typical 99.9% monthly allowance, so I will open an SLA claim and reconcile our logs with yours; if the outage is confirmed we will apply the appropriate service credits to your account. I should keep it concise and check if they need any more details or logs, confirming I've received their timestamps and account ID. **Proposing credit and investigation plan**

I’ll acknowledge any disappointment and apologize while confirming that I've received the timestamps and account ID. rounds.response: Thank you — and I’m sorry for the disruption; I’ve received the three UTC windows and NB-ENT-4472 and will start the investigation now. I’ll prioritize this as an Enterprise Plus claim, reconcile our telemetry with your timestamps/regions, and deliver preliminary findings within 48 hours. If we confirm an SLA breach we will apply the appropriate service credit as an account-level adjustment and it will be visible in your billing portal within 48 hours of confirmation (if it posts after your billing cutoff it may be reflected on the next invoice but the credit itself will show on the account beforehand). rounds.consequence: Your last response, which acknowledged their disappointment, explained why credits aren’t always automatic, committed to prioritized investigation, and promised visibility of any credit in the portal within a defined window, partially restores their confidence but they still feel some frustration about having to initiate the process themselves.
